title: Advice to young bass players: develop your own style
summary: Garland tells young bassists to learn all the beats but find something of their own rather than copy others.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: We just saw a picture of Arvell Arnold, he'll be out in September. He played with Armstrong. I remember Arvell Arnold Shaw from those days. We discussed some of the other bass players, last time. Oh, suppose, what would you tell a youngster who wants to be a bass player, want s to be a jazz bass player. What would you tell him to think about now?

You know a lot of these young bass players they like to take up, say for instance, me, follow me and they follow me on the stand, or follow John Doe, anybody. I always tell them, go to work and try to get something of your own.
I say, don't try to play like the other
guy. Get something of your own don't --
-- go tricking some of his stuff, you understand?
-- but try to get something of your own.
And what else should they do?
And, just pay attention to what he's doing, pay attention to the bass player, any bass player as far as I'm concerned.

If he's just starting out. You understand, and the main thing is to make sure he learns how to give them the rhythm they want. If they want four beats, make sure they learn four beats, in fact, try to play all the beats, four beats and two beats, down to one beat as far as that's concerned.
But make sure to try to get something of your own. Establish your own pattern.
